primitives.name: Observer Agent Activation
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is no standalone "observer" agent type: any agent definition becomes an observer when another agent's frontmatter names it in `observer:`.
primitives.assumptions: Any agent can be configured as an observer via frontmatter declaration; observer status is contextually dependent on observed agent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observer-agent pair is not explicitly defined in frontmatter, activation fails silently.

layer2.mapping: Observer agent activation mirrors dual-space projection in GSI's belief-state tracking, where observer role is encoded in agent metadata rather than runtime type.
layer2.telemetry: Activation event logged in agent lifecycle trace.

primitives.name: Activity Digest Stream
primitives.verbatim_quote: After each of its turns you will receive a read-only activity digest wrapped in <${observedEnvelopeName}-activity> tags.
primitives.assumptions: Digests are immutable, ordered sequences of agent actions; observer receives only read access.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Stream halts if observed agent terminates or digest generation fails.

layer2.mapping: Activity stream serves as kernel for GSE's temporal state transition model, encoding agent behavior as discrete events.
layer2.telemetry: Timestamped digest sequence integrity verified by GSE engine.

primitives.name: Observer Report Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: # ObserverReport tool Send a report to the agent you are observing.
primitives.assumptions: Reports are asynchronous, non-blocking, and delivered via internal queue mechanism.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mechanism fails if target agent is unreachable or report exceeds size limit.

layer2.mapping: ObserverReport maps to GSI's error-correction feedback loop, where observer detects anomalies and propagates corrective signals.
layer2.telemetry: Report delivery confirmed via GSE prompt injection log.

The observer agent architecture embodies a dualistic epistemological framework, wherein one agent observes another without direct participation. This creates a meta-loop: the observer's role is defined by its relationship to the observed, not its intrinsic nature. The activity digest stream provides a causal chain of events that the observer processes in isolation, ensuring no interference with the observed agent’s execution path. The ObserverReport tool introduces a controlled feedback mechanism, allowing the observer to inject insights only when necessary—this aligns with principles of minimal intervention in Bayesian inference and formalized decision theory. The steady-state silence implies a low-information regime, which is optimal for reducing noise in probabilistic reasoning systems. Failure modes include misconfiguration of observer-agent pairs, digest corruption, or report delivery failures, all of which disrupt the integrity of the observation loop.
